about: Scenarios of the publication queue (documentation/Canonical Form.md). Each scenario has a small invented vault, a deny list, and steps. The TypeScript tests and the Rust tests run every step and must get what the step states. Steps: "write" and "delete" change files of the vault. "store" stands for another device: it writes files into the content store and pushes them, also the configuration with its deny list. "status" states the queue. "plan" states the plan of a selection, or that the selection is refused. "publish" makes the plan of a selection and applies it at the time, and states the lists of paths of the report. "expect" states the text of files of the vault and of the content store: null says that the file does not exist. Its "attachmentStorage", when it has one, states every file of the attachment storage, by its key. A file of the vault or of the storage is a text, or {"bytes": ...} with its bytes in hexadecimal. Steps of the failure cases (issue 36): "crash" makes the plan of a selection and applies it, but the run stops at a point, as after a power cut: "write" (the files are written into the copy, before the commit), "commit" (after the commit, before the push) or "push" (after the push, before the correction of the property). It leaves the lock and the journal. "unlock" removes the lock. "offline" makes the content store unreachable, and "online" makes it reachable again. "lose" deletes files of the attachment storage, by their keys, as the cleanup of another device would. A "status" or a "publish" with "refused" states that the command stops. A "plan" states "offline" when the plan uses the last fetch. Every expected value is written by hand. The hashes were computed with sha256sum.
